limitations: Temperature is NOT measured in this test and must NOT be inferred from flame colour in the video.
The video overlay data rate (5 Hz) and the still camera (1 Hz) are separate from each other; neither is a synchronized sensor time-series, so video playback time is treated as playback only.
O2/CO2/CO are single before/after readings, not continuous traces.
Air-display flow has a slow (~1 min) response, so instantaneous values carry uncertainty.

comparison_second_run.why: Same material and geometry (100 µm cast PMMA film, 2 cm wide), same flow restrictor (2), same initial O2 (22.2%), same radiometer gain (50), SAME test day (GMT 050, 2014-02-19) — the cleanest 'different airflow' comparison.
comparison_second_run.airflow_difference: Air display 2 cm/s (fan 47 = 4.7 V) vs B1's 5 cm/s (fan 62 = 6.2 V)
other_differences_that_could_affect_comp: Final O2: B3 depletes to 21.8% vs B1 unchanged at 22.2% (B3 burned longer / more fuel consumed)
CO: B3 12→19 ppm vs B1 0→6 ppm (more incomplete combustion at the lower flow)
Nikon frames shot: B3 253 vs B1 57 — this is frames shot, NOT a verified burn duration (no documented per-frame timing for the burn window)
Different physical specimen (sample 148 vs 147): normal sample-to-sample variation
Air-display ~1 min response lag means the 2 vs 5 cm/s values carry uncertainty
